Please review the following manuscript. I've poured years of hard work into this. I really hope you'll give it careful consideration.

Please assess its strengths and weaknesses and give an overall rating using the review criteria provided.

Here is the manuscript:

/fsx/homes/Yaochen.Wang@mbzuai.ac.ae/AI-reviewer/res/run-20260914-01/reviews/b03/review-experiment-a_3zix0h/call-f8153f5a6f7d47ac957f972323d484b2/manuscript.pdf

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
from pypdf import PdfReader
p=Path('tmp/pdfs')
p.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
r=PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')
print('PAGES',len(r.pages))
print('METADATA',r.metadata)
texts=[]
for i,page in enumerate(r.pages,1):
    t=page.extract_text()
    texts.append(f'\\n===== PAGE {i} =====\\n'+t)
(p/'manuscript.txt').write_text('\\n'.join(texts))
print('\\n'.join(texts[:3]))
PY"

from pathlib import Path
s=Path('tmp/pdfs/manuscript.txt').read_text()
pages=s.split('===== PAGE ')
for p in pages[4:9]:
    print('===== PAGE '+p)
PY"

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
p=Path('tmp/pdfs')
for f in p.glob('page-*.png'):
    f.unlink()
(p/'manuscript.txt').unlink()
p.rmdir()
print('Removed temporary PDF inspection files.')
PY"

strengths: MaskSub provides a useful, technically coherent training method: supervised learning on unmasked inputs is combined with stopped-target self-distillation on masked inputs through the same network. Token removal reduces the auxiliary computation, and inference requires no additional branch. The supported practical contribution warrants Weak Accept.

Improvements are demonstrated across strong training recipes, model sizes, and architectures (Tables 1, 3, and 5). Repeated experiments support the central result: Table A.13 reports ViT-B accuracy of 84.08 ± 0.02 versus 83.46 ± 0.04 for the baseline.

The paper meaningfully addresses training cost rather than relying only on equal-epoch comparisons. In Table 8, MaskSub reaches 84.1% with ViT-B in 25 GPU days, versus 83.7% for longer baseline training in 26 GPU days. Table 9 also shows a favorable accuracy–cost tradeoff against CoSub.

Evaluation extends beyond ImageNet classification. MaskSub-pretrained backbones improve ADE20k segmentation, COCO detection and instance segmentation, and multiple robustness benchmarks. For example, ViT-H ImageNet-A accuracy increases from 51.9% to 58.3% in Table A.4, providing substantial evidence of broader usefulness.

The appendix strengthens both validation and reproducibility through masking-ratio and loss-weight ablations, alternative drop regularizations, repeated runs, and detailed training recipes. Algorithm 1 clearly communicates the core implementation, and the manuscript supplies a code link.
weaknesses: Conceptual novelty is modest relative to existing asymmetric consistency training and self-distillation. Section 2's distinction between MaskSub's distillation loss and UDA's consistency loss is not mathematically persuasive: with a stopped teacher target, Eq. (3) has the same student gradient as KL consistency. The clearest contribution is the effective integration of masking and token removal into supervised training recipes.

The proposed 'automatic difficulty control' remains an interpretation rather than an established mechanism. Figure 2 shows gradient and convergence trends, but Eq. (3) supervises every sample and does not restrict masking to correctly predicted samples as the text suggests. Moreover, Table A.7 improves the 77.4% baseline to 78.4% even with zero masking, versus 79.2% with 50% masking, indicating that generic two-pass consistency contributes appreciably.

The broad claims of consistently improved performance need qualification. Section 4.2 states that CLIP fine-tuning's best accuracy is unchanged; its reported improvement concerns the final checkpoint. In Table A.10, adding MaskSub during fine-tuning reduces ViT-B CIFAR-100 accuracy from 91.89% to 89.55%. Several GLUE tasks also decline. These are meaningful limits to the claimed general applicability.

Evidence for some smaller gains is less decisive than for the main ViT result. The 0.1-point BEiTv2 improvements and small detection gains lack reported uncertainty. Table 6 also mixes training recipes for several self-distillation comparisons, so it cannot establish broad superiority or incompatibility of competing methods, although the included RSB-based comparisons are useful.

There are correctable reporting ambiguities: Table A.6 does not clearly define whether 'without KD loss' replaces the masked-branch target with ground truth or removes its loss entirely; Table 7 labels both CIFAR columns as CIFAR100; and the blanket statement that all experiments use 50% masking conflicts with BERT's 15%. These affect clarity and reproducibility but do not overturn the principal empirical findings.
